headline: First batch of 18 new railway coaches arrive from India
summary: The broad-gauge passenger coaches entered Bangladesh via the Darshana international rail link on Friday afternoon.
details: The first shipment of 18 new broad-gauge passenger railway coaches imported from India has arrived in Bangladesh. The coaches entered the country through the Darshana international railway line in Chuadanga on Friday afternoon.

The shipment consists of four types of coaches: 11 non-AC Shovon chairs, three AC chairs, two AC sleepers, and two AC power cars. The power cars include separate compartments for guards and luggage storage.

Project Director Joydul Islam took charge of the coaches upon arrival. Following customs clearance and official formalities at Darshana station, the coaches are being transported to the Syedpur Railway Workshop in Nilphamari.
At the Syedpur workshop, the coaches will undergo technical processes, including initial connection setup and performance testing, before being integrated into the passenger train fleet.
These coaches are being procured through India's RITES Limited as part of a larger agreement between Bangladesh and India to supply a total of 200 broad-gauge railway coaches.
Divisional Mechanical Engineer Rabiul Islam stated that initial inspections showed no defects, and he expects the coaches to operate smoothly without major mechanical issues.
caption:
18 new railway coaches have just arrived from India! 🚆

The first shipment of 18 new broad-gauge passenger railway coaches imported from India has arrived in Bangladesh. The coaches entered the country through the Darshana international railway line in Chuadanga on Friday afternoon.

The shipment consists of four types of coaches: 11 non-AC Shovon chairs, three AC chairs, two AC sleepers, and two AC power cars. The power cars include separate compartments for guards and luggage storage.

Project Director Joydul Islam took charge of the coaches upon arrival. Following customs clearance and official formalities at Darshana station, the coaches are being transported to the Syedpur Railway Workshop in Nilphamari.

At the Syedpur workshop, the coaches will undergo technical processes, including initial connection setup and performance testing, before being integrated into the passenger train fleet.

These coaches are being procured through India's RITES Limited as part of a larger agreement between Bangladesh and India to supply a total of 200 broad-gauge railway coaches.

Divisional Mechanical Engineer Rabiul Islam stated that initial inspections showed no defects, and he expects the coaches to operate smoothly without major mechanical issues.
